name: Impacket GetUserSPNs - Request TGS Hashes
description: Requests TGS-REP tickets for all SPN accounts and saves hashcat-ready hashes to file. The DC hands over encrypted tickets — the encryption IS the attack surface. Use -request-user <name> to target a single high-value account.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHAT THIS DOES MECHANICALLY ===
GetUserSPNs.py -request does two things in one:
  1. LDAP query to find all accounts with SPNs (same as list mode)
  2. KDC request (AS-REQ + TGS-REQ) for each SPN found

The DC responds with a TGS ticket encrypted with the service account's NT hash.
The tool extracts the $krb5tgs$ encrypted blob and formats it for Hashcat.

=== HASH FORMAT IN OUTPUT FILE ===
  $krb5tgs$23$*sqldev$INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL$MSSQLSvc/DEV-PRE-SQL...${hex}:${hex}
The $23$ means RC4 encryption (etype 23) — the crackable-faster mode.
AES256 shows as $18$ and is MUCH slower to crack (mode 19700 vs 13100).

=== TARGETED vs BULK ROASTING ===
  -request            → roasts ALL SPN accounts (noisier; more Event 4769 logs)
  -request-user NAME  → roasts one account (quieter; prioritize high-value targets)
  Strategy: list first (-no -request), pick accounts with admincount=1 or
  old PasswordLastSet, then roast just those with -request-user.

=== ENCRYPTION TYPE MATTERS ===
RC4 (etype 23, hashcat mode 13100)    → fast crack, default on older DCs
AES256 (etype 18, hashcat mode 19700) → slow crack; preferred by newer DCs
Check encryption type: Get-DomainUser testspn -Properties msds-supportedencryptiontypes
If account supports RC4, you can force RC4 with Rubeus /rc4opsec flag.

=== AFTER ROASTING ===
  hashcat -m 13100 <outfile> /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
  hashcat -m 13100 <outfile> /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r best64.rule
Verify cracked password: crackmapexec smb <dc_ip> -u sqldev -p database!

=== DETECTION FOOTPRINT ===
Event ID 4769 (Kerberos TGS Request) — one per ticket requested
KerberosRequestorSecurityToken type, encryption downgrade to RC4 = suspicious
Many 4769s in short time for service accounts = Kerberoasting detected Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication).

defense.why_it_works: impacket GetUserSPNs -request requests TGS tickets for SPN accounts from Linux and outputs their crackable hashes.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain credentials and network access to the DC.
defense.impact: Crackable TGS hashes for the domain's service accounts.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558.003] Event 4769 (TGS requested) with RC4 encryption type (0x17) when AES is standard, or a burst of TGS requests for many SPNs from one source in a short window; a request for a honeypot SPN account is malicious by definition.
defense.artifacts: 4769 TGS requests (often RC4); the extracted hashes.
defense.prevention: Use 100+ character passwords or gMSA for service accounts; disable RC4 (force AES); audit and remove unused SPNs; deploy honeypot SPN accounts to catch roasting; Defender for Identity flags mass TGS requests.
defense.evasion: Rubeus can force an RC4 downgrade (/rc4opsec, /tgtdeleg) to obtain crackable tickets even where AES is preferred; request one SPN at a time to stay under the bulk-4769 threshold.
defense.misconfiguration: Service accounts are registered with a Service Principal Name (SPN) but use weak, human-chosen passwords — or even share a password with other accounts. Any authenticated domain user can request a TGS for any SPN account, receiving a blob encrypted with that account's NTLM hash. The SPN registration itself is not the flaw; the flaw is weak passwords on SPN accounts and permitting RC4 encryption (which produces a shorter, faster-to-crack blob).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service account set up manually with a weak password + SPN
# Attacker can find these with:
Get-ADUser -Filter {ServicePrincipalName -ne '$null'} -Properties ServicePrincipalName,PasswordLastSet

# Bad state — password set 4 years ago, RC4 permitted:
# Name: svc_sql  PasswordLastSet: 2020-01-15  SPN: MSSQLSvc/db01.corp.local:1433
# RC4 (0x17) requested in TGS ticket — short hash, GPU-crackable

# Confirming RC4 is available:
Get-ADUser svc_sql -Properties msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes
# msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes: 0 (= RC4+AES both permitted if 0 or blank)
defense.secure_config:
# Fix 1 — Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA): 240-char random passwords,
# auto-rotated by AD, no human ever knows the password
New-ADServiceAccount -Name gmsa_sql -DNSHostName sql.corp.local \
    -PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword 'db-servers-grp'
Install-ADServiceAccount gmsa_sql

# Fix 2 — For legacy accounts that must keep SPNs:
# Set a 100+ character random password (AD max is 127 chars):
$pw = [System.Web.Security.Membership]::GeneratePassword(127,20)
Set-ADAccountPassword svc_sql -NewPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString $pw -AsPlainText -Force)

# Fix 3 — Disable RC4, require AES-only:
Set-ADUser svc_sql -KerberosEncryptionType AES128,AES256
# msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 24 (AES128+AES256 only)
